pylint_messages.reason: The default list is created once and shared by every call of add_order, so orders leak between unrelated calls. This is a real correctness bug and should be fixed by using None as the default.
The else after return is unnecessary and makes the function slightly harder to read, but the result is still correct. It is a genuine style issue with low priority, so it can be cleaned up later.

review_vs_tool.explanation: The formula is valid Python; only the docstring shows it returns the discount instead of the discounted price, and pylint does not compare code with docstrings.
Multiplying two numbers is legal code, so pylint cannot know the base amount should have been added.
A mutable default argument is a fixed code pattern that pylint checks for directly (W0102).
Choosing > instead of >= is a boundary decision from the specification, which pylint does not know.
The unnecessary else after return is a structural pattern that pylint recognises (R1705), although it cannot see the missing input validation.
The division by zero only happens at runtime for an empty list, and pylint does not track the possible values of len(numbers).
Returning low is a valid variable reference, so the wrong value is only visible by understanding what clamp should do.
range(1, n) is a correct call; the off-by-one error depends on the meaning of factorial, not on Python rules.
Checking membership in a lowercase string is valid code, and pylint cannot read the docstring requirement to ignore case.
The slice limit - 1 is syntactically fine, so the off-by-one boundary error is invisible to a static style checker.
